correction_note: CITATION AND LICENSE CONFIRMED, ELONGATE CLAIM CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED. Author list, title and venue match the authors' own BibTeX in the 3DAnimals README verbatim: @InProceedings{wu2023magicpony, author = {Wu, Shangzhe and Li, Ruining and Jakab, Tomas and Rupprecht, Christian and Vedaldi, Andrea}, booktitle = {CVPR}, year = {2023}}. MIT license verified on both repos. ONE REFINEMENT TO THE RECORD'S ELONGATE CLAIM, and it makes the finding BETTER, not worse: the record described birds and quadrupeds as two hard-coded heuristic BRANCHES. In the actual code they are not separate branches at all. I read magicpony/geometry/skinning.py::estimate_bones and both configs. The body-bone construction is IDENTICAL for birds and horses — both use body_bones_mode: z_minmax_y+, which takes argmax/argmin of the z-coordinate over vertices above the mesh midpoint's y, then interpolates a chain of joints between those two extreme points through the centroid. The ONLY difference is num_legs: 0 (bird) vs num_legs: 4 + num_leg_bones: 3 (horse); when n_leg_bones is not > 0 the leg block is skipped entirely and all_bones = bones_pred, i.e. body chain only. So obtaining an axial-chain skeleton for a sevengill is literally a one-value config edit (num_legs: 0), not a code fork. The record's quoted phrasings ('chain of bones through the two farthest end points along the z-axis'; legs to 'the lowest point in each quadrant') are accurate paraphrases of real code — I confirmed the quadrant code (quadrant0 = torch.logical_and(xs > x_margin, zs > 0), etc.) and the 'find a point with the lowest y in each quadrant' comment — but they are parameterised, not branched. correction_note: CITATION CONFIRMED; TWO SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD. (1) CODE URL IS MISLEADING AS GIVEN. The record lists 'https://github.com/KeqiangSun/Ponymation ; also in https://github.com/3DAnimals/3DAnimals (MIT)', implying the first is the primary release and the second a mirror. I fetched KeqiangSun/Ponymation: it exists and is public, but it is a README-only placeholder — roughly six commits, a paper blurb, a OneDrive link to the AnimalMotion Dataset, and NO implementation files. The record's license line ('No license shown in the Ponymation repo sidebar — verified, none displayed') is literally true but buries the real point, which is that there is nothing there to license. The usable, MIT-licensed implementation is 3DAnimals/3DAnimals, which contains the full ponymation module, config/model/ponymation.yaml and eight stage1/stage2 training configs. The lab should point at 3DAnimals only. (2) THE ELONGATE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AND I HAVE DOWNGRADED IT. The record asserts Ponymation 'inherits MagicPony's bone heuristics (so the bird/axial-chain branch is available)'. Half true. The skinning code IS shared, and num_legs is a parameter there, so num_legs: 0 is expressible. But config/model/ponymation.yaml explicitly sets num_legs: 4 and num_leg_bones: 3, and I enumerated the entire config directory: the Ponymation configs cover horse, cow, giraffe and zebra ONLY. MagicPony ships a bird config; Ponymation does not. So unlike MagicPony — where an axial chain is a released, pretrained, one-value config change — for Ponymation the axial-chain setting has never been trained or demonstrated with the motion VAE. Calling it 'available' overstates readiness; it is expressible but unvalidated. The record's underlying intuition still stands and is the reason to keep this paper: a LEARNED generative motion prior is exactly what would regularize an anguilliform sevengill fit across frames, and it is the direct analogue of the lab's BiLSTM+Skeletor temporal stage — but it would have to be trained from scratch on sevengill video, with the added unknown that the transformer VAE's 10-frame clips and 8-bone chain were tuned for quadruped gaits, not for a continuous travelling-wave body undulation. (3) MINOR TITLE NOTE: the canonical ECCV title includes 'Articulated', per the authors' own BibTeX (@InProceedings{sun2024ponymation, title = {{Ponymation}: Learning Articulated 3D Animal Motions from Unlabeled Online Videos}, booktitle = {ECCV}, year = {2024}}), and the six-author list matches the record exactly. RigNet is vendored at third_party/RigNet and is GPL-3.0 upstream (zhan-xu/RigNet: sidebar 'GPL-3.0 license', LICENSE-GPLv3.txt, README 'This project is under LICENSE-GPLv3'), which is almost certainly WHY CAMM's root license is GPLv3. The NON-COMMERCIAL restriction is real but comes from a different place than the record said: CAMM's README states 'Our code is mainly built based on BANMo', and facebookresearch/banmo is CC-BY-NC 4.0. NET EFFECT FOR THE LAB: strong copyleft (GPL-3.0) PLUS an inherited non-commercial encumbrance (CC-BY-NC-4.0 via BANMo) — and those two are mutually incompatible for redistribution, so this codebase is research-use-only in practice and cannot cleanly ship in any product. (2) RigNet SKELETONIZATION of that canonical mesh via third_party/RigNet/extract_skel.py to produce a kinematic chain plus skinning weights, followed by kinematic-chain-aware re-optimization. The README notes bandwidth and threshold may need tuning to get a good chain.
supervision: Monocular video. Preprocessing per BANMo format: detectron2 segmentation masks; optical flow from VCN-robust computed between every {1,2,4,8,16,32} frames; DINO-ViT features (compute_dino.py, dim 16); AND 16-dim DensePose features from CSE.

Per-video preprocessing required: detectron2 masks + VCN-robust optical flow at 6 frame gaps {1,2,4,8,16,32} + 16-dim DINO features + 16-dim CSE DensePose features. Custom data is supplied as .mp4 RGB videos. Marching-cubes resolution 256 (mesh extraction, NOT training image resolution). NOT STATED anywhere in the repo docs: number of videos, number of frames per video, training image resolution, batch size, number of epochs/rounds, or total optimization time/GPU-hours. IMAGES PER INDIVIDUAL / VIEWS: monocular video of one subject per model; the method builds a per-subject model, so 'views' come from subject and camera motion over the clip rather than a calibrated rig — the count is not quantified in the docs.

elongate_relevance: HIGH — CAMM assumes no body plan at all: the kinematic chain is discovered by RigNet skeletonization of whatever canonical mesh stage 1 recovers, and its working demos include a serial-chain robot arm and an eagle, neither of which is a quadruped.
correction_note: CITATION CONFIRMED (authors, title, venue all correct) BUT TIGHTENED, AND THE LICENSE FIELD WAS WRONG. (1) LICENSE — the record said 'CC BY-NC 4.0 for the project, with GPLv3 for the bundled RigNet component (verified by fetching LICENSE)'. That is backwards, and the 'verified' tag on it was not earned. I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kts707/camm/main/LICENSE and it opens 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007' — the PROJECT is GPL-3.0. The CC-BY-NC-4.0 comes from BANMo, the upstream CAMM is built on, not from CAMM's own license text. The record's bottom-line 'NON-COMMERCIAL' conclusion happens to be right, but for the wrong reason, and the reason matters: GPL-3.0 copyleft and CC-BY-NC-4.0 are incompatible to combine and redistribute, so this is the most legally encumbered of the four records and the lab should treat it as read-and-learn-from, not build-on-and-ship. (2) CITATION FORM — corrected to the official CVF Workshops form from the repo's own BibTeX, including page range 6586-6596 and the official capitalization 'From' (@InProceedings{Kuai_2023_CVPR, booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) Workshops}, month = {June}, year = {2023}, pages = {6586-6596}}). The repo README contains NO arxiv.org link at all, so arXiv:2304.06937 as carried in the record is UNVERIFIED — arxiv.org is egress-blocked here and I could not check it. Flagging rather than silently keeping it. (3) TWO ADDITIONS THE RECORD MISSED, both decision-relevant. FIRST, CAMM's demos are not just human + robot arm: docs/DATA.md also covers an EAGLE dataset (animated mesh sequences, inherited from BANMo). A bird is a second non-quadruped demo and it strengthens the record's argument that skeleton topology is genuinely discovered rather than assumed. SECOND, AND THIS IS A CONCRETE BLOCKER THE RECORD DID NOT FLAG: CAMM's preprocessing requires '16-dim DensePose features from CSE'. That is the same Continuous Surface Embeddings line the lab's research question is built around — but CSE models exist for humans and a fixed set of mammal classes, and there is NO CSE/DensePose model for any elasmobranch. So running CAMM on sevengill video means either dropping the CSE channel entirely and relying on DINO features alone, or first solving the very problem the lab is asking about. The record's recommended experiment (stage 1 on sevengill video, then RigNet on the canonical mesh, then inspect the chain) is still the right first move, but it has to be run in a CSE-free configuration and that is an untested path. (4) The record's core claim — that CAMM is the one method in this family with no hard-wired body plan, and that a robot arm is a serial chain topologically closer to a shark than a dog is — is CONFIRMED, and the vendored extract_skel.py entry point the record cites is real (README links directly to third_party/RigNet/extract_skel.py#L457).

citation: Peter Kulits, Michael J. Black, Silvia Zuffi. "Reconstructing Animals and the Wild." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2025. representation_3d: Per the official repo README (fetched verbatim): 'We train an LLM to decode a frozen CLIP embedding of a natural image into a structured compositional scene representation encompassing both animals and their habitats.' The candidate's added specifics — autoregressive decoding to graphics code, a scene graph over SMAL-based animal assets, ~1M synthetic training images, thousands of assets — are NOT confirmed; the README states none of them and the paper/project page are unreachable. The 'is not a new body model / composes existing assets' framing IS consistent with the README's own one-sentence summary.
supervision: Single image -> frozen CLIP embedding -> LLM decoder -> structured scene representation. Confirmed from the README summary sentence. Training is on a rendered/synthetic corpus (implied by the tar/feather train+val split shipped by the project page); the exact corpus size is not stated in any reachable source.
species_domain: Wildlife scenes (animals plus habitat). The SMAL-family quadruped-asset claim is plausible given the Zuffi/Black authorship but is NOT confirmed from any reachable source.
data_requirement: Partially concrete, from the README's training command (fetched): --max_steps 40000, batch size passed as --per_device_train_batch_size (value left as a placeholder 'X'), --image_aspect_ratio pad. environment.yml (fetched) pins pytorch-cuda=12.1 and includes deepspeed, xformers, bitsandbytes and peft — i.e. multi-GPU sharded LLM fine-tuning, LLaVA-derived. Training data ships as data/train.tar + data/train.gz.feather (images + tabular scene annotations) with a matching val split. NOT STATED anywhere reachable: number of training images, number of assets, image resolution, GPU count, GPU-hours, images per individual, number of views. The candidate's '~1M images and thousands of assets' is UNVERIFIED — do not cite that number.
key_numbers: not obtainable — no benchmark metrics were readable from any reachable source. Only the training-length figure (40,000 optimizer steps) is verified.
elongate_relevance: low — it composes pre-existing (quadruped, SMAL-family) assets rather than modelling a new body plan, so it offers a sevengill nothing on articulation, and its non-commercial MPI license plus registration-gated data make it a poor dependency; its only transferable value is as a precedent for large synthetic-render training pipelines, which the lab already runs in Blender for SharkSMPL.
correction_note: The citation as given was ACCURATE and is now confirmed from two independent fetched sources: (1) https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kulits/RAW/master/README.md, the authors' own repo, which titles the work 'Reconstructing Animals and the Wild' and lists exactly Peter Kulits, Michael J. citation: Ci Li, Yi Yang, Zehang Weng, Elin Hernlund, Silvia Zuffi, Hedvig Kjellström. "Dessie: Disentanglement for Articulated 3D Horse Shape and Pose Estimation from Images." Asian Conference on Computer Vision (ACCV) 2024. arXiv:2410.03438
license: MIT for the code — VERIFIED by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Celiali/Dessie/main/LICENSE: standard MIT text, 'Copyright (c) 2024 Ci Li', permission to 'use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell'. NO non-commercial clause on the code. HOWEVER the hSMAL body model is NOT in the repo: the README directs users to obtain it from the CV4Horses Google Site (https://sites.google.com/view/cv4horses/cv4horses) plus a Google Drive file, so it carries its own separate terms. Those hSMAL terms could NOT be read (sites.google.com is blocked by the egress proxy) — treat hSMAL as SMAL-derived and therefore presumptively non-commercial/registration-gated until someone reads that page. The same caveat applies to the PFERD pose data (Harvard Dataverse, doi 10.7910/DVN/2EXONE) and the TEXTure-derived texture maps.
representation_3d: hSMAL (horse-specific SMAL) mesh with linear blend skinning, driven by disentangled latent codes. The repo's pretrained-weights layout (fetched) confirms the disentanglement framing operationally: two model families, DESSIE and a DinoHMR baseline, each in a TOTALRANDOM variant ('only trained on synthetic data', annotated in the README as 'trained w/o $L_gt$') and a COMBINAREAL variant ('finetune on MagicPony dataset'). The training script confirms the ablation is real: --GT --W_gt_shape 0. --W_gt_pose 0. --W_gt_trans 0., i.e. the ground-truth supervision weights are literally zeroed.
supervision: Synthetic-only training via an on-the-fly renderer the authors call DessiePIPE, composed from three fetched-and-confirmed ingredients: pose sequences derived from PFERD (the authors' own equine mocap dataset, Li et al., Scientific Data 11(1):497, 2024), texture maps derived from TEXTure (text-driven texture generation), and COCO 2017 images as randomized backgrounds. Optional finetuning on real images from MagicPony or the Staths/animals3d corpus. Evaluated with keypoint transfer, PCK/IoU/AUC on Animal Pose and Pascal, PCK and PA-MPJPE on PFERD, and Chamfer distance on PFERD against MagicPony and 3D-Fauna.
species_domain: Horses (hSMAL). The candidate's claim that it 'generalizes to zebras, cows, deer' is NOT stated anywhere in the README and is UNVERIFIED — the paper is unreachable. Do not repeat it as fact.
data_requirement: The most concrete numbers in this chunk, all read from the actual SLURM training script https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Celiali/Dessie/main/code/script/train_dessie_1.sh: #SBATCH --gpus 2, #SBATCH -t 3-00:00:00 (3-day wall clock, i.e. an upper bound of ~144 GPU-hours for one synthetic-only run), #SBATCH --mem 50G, --imgsize 256 (256x256 input), --batch_size 16 with --data_batch_size 2, --max-epochs 800, --useinterval 8 (pose-sequence subsampling), --DINO_model_name dino_vits8 (DINOv1 ViT-S/8 backbone), --background --background_path .../syndata/coco, --getPairs (paired-sample disentanglement). Environment: Python 3.7, PyTorch 1.11.0+cu113, Ubuntu 18. Training-set SIZE in images is NOT stated — DessiePIPE renders on the fly, so there is no fixed image count; likewise images-per-individual, number of views and GPU-hours-to-convergence are not stated. This 2-GPU / 3-day / 256px figure is a useful order-of-magnitude anchor for scoping a sevengill equivalent.
key_numbers: not obtainable — the README reports no metric values (it only names the evaluation protocols: PCK, IoU, AUC, PA-MPJPE, Chamfer distance). The paper PDF is unreachable, so no headline numbers can be quoted honestly.
elongate_relevance: medium — the animal is a quadruped and hSMAL is useless for a hexanchiform, but methodologically this is the closest published template for what a sevengill model would have to do: train a SMAL-family regressor purely on domain-randomized synthetic renders with shape/pose/APPEARANCE explicitly disentangled, which is exactly the axis the pose-invariant re-ID hypothesis needs (marginalize pose, keep appearance as identity) and exactly the training strategy shark-pose-3d already uses.
correction_note: Every field of this record that I could check held up, and the record's 'confidence: verified' was earned. Confirmed by fetching the official repo README verbatim: the title, the six-author list in exact order (Ci Li, Yi Yang, Zehang Weng, Elin Hernlund, Silvia Zuffi, Hedvig Kjellström), the venue line 'ACCV 2024', and the repo's own BibTeX (@inproceedings{li2024dessie, booktitle={Asian Conference on Computer Vision}, year={2024}). MIT license confirmed by reading the LICENSE file itself, not the sidebar badge. THREE ADDITIONS/SHARPENINGS: (1) the backbone is dino_vits8 — DINOv1 ViT-S/8, NOT DINOv2 — which matters because the lab's SharkScarAnnotator and shark-scar-classifier are built on DINOv2 ViT-S/14; the comparison to DinoHMR in this repo is therefore a v1-era baseline. (2) The record said the hSMAL model is 'a separate download under its own (non-commercial) terms' — the separate-download part is CONFIRMED from the README, but the non-commercial characterization is an INFERENCE I could not verify, because sites.google.com is blocked; report it as 'SMAL-derived, terms unread, presume restricted'. (3) The 'generalizes to zebras, cows, deer' claim is unsupported by anything reachable and should be dropped or flagged. Note also the useful downstream pointer in the README: Dessie's own evaluation harness contains ready-made comparison plumbing against MagicPony and 3D-Fauna, which are separate seed-reference targets for this scan.

citation: Jin Lyu, Liang An, Li Lin, Pujin Cheng, Yebin Liu, Xiaoying Tang. "AniMer+: Unified Pose and Shape Estimation Across Mammalia and Aves via Family-Aware Transformer." arXiv:2508.00298, 2025. "AniMer: Animal Pose and Shape Estimation Using Family Aware Transformer." CVPR 2025, pp. 17486-17496. arXiv:2412.00837
venue: arXiv preprint; IEEE TPAMI 2025 author-asserted but unverified (predecessor AniMer is confirmed CVPR 2025)
code_url: https://github.com/AniMerPlus/AniMerPlus (canonical, 28 stars, topics: 3d-reconstruction, animal). license: MIT — VERIFIED for BOTH repos by fetching the LICENSE files directly, not the sidebar badge. AniMer+: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AniMerPlus/AniMerPlus/master/LICENSE, standard MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2025 AniMerPlus'. AniMer: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luoxue-star/AniMer/master/LICENSE, standard MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2024 Jin Lv'. Default branch is master, not main, for both. CAVEAT THAT SURVIVES: neither README says anything about the terms of the underlying SMAL / AVES parametric models or of the checkpoint and dataset files, all of which are distributed via Google Drive links rather than under the MIT repo. What IS verified from the fetched READMEs is the lineage: both repos state that code is borrowed from ViTPose, 4DHumans, HaMer and SupContrast — i.e. a ViT-backbone HMR-style regressor with a supervised-contrastive objective, which is consistent with (but not proof of) the family-aware/taxa-discriminative framing.

AniMer's README (fetched) names its training corpus CtrlAni3D and requires it to be reformatted to match the Animal3D annotation schema. AniMer+ generalizes the same recipe across Mammalia and Aves. AniMer's README also carries an honest-error note worth recording: 'we found that the 3D keypoints of the Animal3D dataset may have been exported incorrectly, so the version released now is the result of retraining after we fixed it' — the paper-reproduction weights live on a separate 'paper' branch.
species_domain: Mammalia and Aves. NOT fish, NOT elasmobranchs — confirmed by the title and by the absence of any aquatic species anywhere in either repo.
data_requirement: Weak. What is VERIFIED from the fetched READMEs: Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.4.0 + torchvision 0.19.0 with CUDA 12.4, pytorch3d built from source, Hydra-configured training launched as `python main.py exp_name=AniMerPlus experiment=AniMerPlus trainer=gpu launcher=local`, Ubuntu (WSL supported via a community fork). Datasets and pretrained backbone are Google Drive downloads. NOT STATED ANYWHERE REACHABLE: the size of CtrlAni3D or CtrlAVES3D, input resolution, batch size, number of GPUs, GPU-hours, images per individual, number of views. THE CANDIDATE'S '~10k quadruped images' AND '~7k bird images' ARE UNVERIFIED — I could not source those figures from the repos, and a GitHub code search for 'CtrlAni3D' returned only two incidental hits (a third-party repo, AdaptiveMotorControlLab/FMPose3D, whose dataset readme says 'Put Animal3D and CtrlAni3D datasets in this folder'), while 'CtrlAVES3D' returned ZERO hits across all of GitHub. Do not put those numbers in the final report as facts; if the scoping argument needs them, mark them explicitly as unconfirmed.
key_numbers: not obtainable — neither README reports any metric. The only verified number in this record is the CVPR 2025 proceedings page range for the predecessor, 17486-17496.
elongate_relevance: medium — it is the field's most explicit attempt to span more than one body plan in a single network, and it stops at two (quadruped mammal, bird), which is itself the finding: cross-body-plan generalization here is bought by adding a whole new parametric model plus a whole new synthetic dataset per taxon, so a hexanchiform with seven gill slits, one posterior dorsal and an anguilliform trunk would need exactly that, not a fine-tune.
correction_note: THE RECORD'S CITATION WAS DEFECTIVE IN TWO WAYS AND IS NOW FIXED. (1) The author placeholder 'AniMer+ authors (see arXiv:2508.00298)' is not a citation. citation: Urs Waldmann, Ole Johannsen, Bastian Goldluecke. "Neural Texture Puppeteer: A Framework for Neural Geometry and Texture Rendering of Articulated Shapes, Enabling Re-Identification at Interactive Speed." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) Workshops, January 2024, pp. 69-79 (CV4Smalls workshop, oral). arXiv:2311.17109. Predecessor: Urs Waldmann et al., "Neural Puppeteer: Keypoint-Based Neural Rendering of Dynamic Shapes", ACCV 2022.
license: MIT (VERIFIED for BOTH repos). NeTePu: LICENSE file present in the repo tree, sidebar reads "MIT license". NePu: sidebar reads "MIT license". This is a permissive, commercially usable license — a genuine advantage over the SMAL/SMPL family, which is research/non-commercial + registration-gated. NOTE the auxiliary assets are more restrictive in practice: Human3.6M requires a login/EULA (vision.imar.ro), and the NePuMoo dataset + pretrained weights are Zenodo-hosted (zenodo.org/records/10402817 and /10402116) whose licenses I could NOT verify — Zenodo is blocked from this session.
representation_3d: Two decoupled pipelines. GEOMETRY: keypoint-conditioned neural renderer (encoder latent dim 1024, local/decoder latent 256, keypoint bottleneck 128, hidden dim 256, "nepu" decoder+renderer architecture) producing depth maps, silhouette masks and NNOPCS maps. TEXTURE: a separate texture auto-encoder trained on color maps that emits a GLOBAL TEXTURE LATENT CODE used as the identity descriptor. Supports novel-pose and novel-view synthesis. CRITICAL DESIGN POINT, and the record framed this correctly: identity is a global latent conditioned on geometry — there is NO UV atlas and NO surface unwrapping anywhere in this method. It is the alternative pole to canonical-UV re-ID, not an instance of it.
supervision: Ground-truth 3D keypoints plus multi-view supervision (silhouette, keypoint, depth and regularization losses; loss weights 3 / 2 / 1 / 0.0625 in the released nepu_geometry.yaml) for the geometry stage; multi-view textured color renders for the texture auto-encoder. Strongly supervised and rig-dependent, NOT in-the-wild monocular.
species_domain: Synthetic cattle (NePuMoo, the paper's own released dataset) plus, in the released configs, synthetic giraffes, pigeons and humans, and real Human3.6M. All quadruped / biped / bird. No aquatic species, no elongate species.
data_requirement: Read directly from the released configs/data_configs.yaml, so these are hard numbers from the code, not from the paper: COWS (NePuMoo) 25 keypoints, 24 CAMERA VIEWS, 910 datapoints; GIRAFFES 26 kps, 24 views, 1900 datapoints; PIGEONS 19 kps, 56 VIEWS, 1450 datapoints; HUMANS 33 kps, 24 views, 3213 datapoints; H36M 32 kps, 4 views, 910 datapoints. Training hyperparameters (nepu_geometry.yaml / nepu_texture_cows.yaml): batch size 64, lr 5e-4, weight decay 0.005, grad clip 1.0, 1500 renderer points, 500 object-renderer points. IMAGE RESOLUTION: not stated in the README or in any released config. GPU / GPU-hours: not stated anywhere in the repo. Images per individual and number of re-ID identities: not stated in any source I could reach (the paper PDF is on arXiv and CVF openaccess, both blocked). THE DECISION-RELEVANT NUMBER IS 24 SYNCHRONIZED CALIBRATED CAMERA VIEWS with ground-truth 3D keypoints. That is a captive multi-camera rig regime. The lab's 661GB corpus is monocular in-the-wild video from 4 CA sites — it does not remotely satisfy this input contract, and nothing in the repo shows a monocular-only training path.
key_numbers: WACV Workshops 2024, pp. 69-79. Latent dims 1024 / 256 / 128. Cow config: 25 keypoints, 24 views, 910 datapoints. Claimed "interactive speed" rendering. Actual re-identification accuracy figures: NOT OBTAINED — I could not fetch the paper, and neither the README nor the project page (urs-waldmann.github.io, blocked) was reachable. Do not quote any re-ID accuracy for this paper without fetching the PDF.
elongate_relevance: medium — keypoint-driven and body-plan-agnostic in principle (no quadruped skeleton is baked in; you supply nkps and camera count per species), and it is genuinely the only work in this chunk built explicitly FOR re-identification, but every released asset is a quadruped/biped/bird at 19-33 keypoints, and the 24-56 synchronized-view training requirement is disqualifying for wild sevengill footage.
correction_note: THREE corrections. (1) CODE URL WAS WRONG. The record pointed at github.com/urs-waldmann/NePu (the ACCV 2022 predecessor) and asserted the NeTePu repo was unverified/nonexistent. The actual repo for THIS paper is github.com/urs-waldmann/NeTePu, created 2023-11-18, description "Code for 'Neural Texture Puppeteer' (WACV Workshop 'CV4Smalls' 2024, oral)", topics animals/applications/neural-rendering/re-identification, last updated 2026-02-23. (2) AUTHORS. The record said "Urs Waldmann et al."; the canonical author list from the repo's own BibTeX is Waldmann, Urs; Johannsen, Ole; Goldluecke, Bastian — only three authors, so "et al." is inappropriate. Pages 69-79 added. (3) PROJECT PAGE. The record gave exc.uni-konstanz.de; the repo links urs-waldmann.github.io/NeTePu (both blocked from here, so neither is confirmed live). LICENSE now VERIFIED as MIT where the record said "Not verified". UNVERIFIED CLAIM TO FLAG: the record asserts the paper "demonstrates a synthetic-to-real texture domain shift to reconstruct texture from a single real RGB image." I could NOT verify this — it is not in the README and the paper is unreachable. The README only says the method "demonstrates applicability to both synthetic data and real-world scenarios through domain adaptation techniques." Do not put the single-RGB-image claim in the final report until the PDF is read. Verification route: fetched github.com/urs-waldmann/NeTePu (sidebar + file tree + BibTeX), github.com/urs-waldmann/NePu (sidebar), raw README.md, and raw configs/data_configs.yaml, configs/nepu_geometry.yaml, configs/nepu_texture_cows.yaml. arXiv abs page NOT fetched (arxiv.org blocked).

citation: Daniele Baieri, Riccardo Cicciarella, Michael Krützen, Emanuele Rodolà, Silvia Zuffi. "Model-based Metric 3D Shape and Motion Reconstruction of Wild Bottlenose Dolphins in Drone-Shot Videos." International Journal of Computer Vision 134(6): 293, 2026. DOI: 10.1007/s11263-026-02906-z. Preprint arXiv:2504.15782 (cs.CV; cs.GR; ACM classes I.4.8, J.3), announced 23 April 2025, 9 pages, 7 figures.
venue: International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV), vol. 134, no. 6, art. 293
license: n/a — no code located, so no license to read.
representation_3d: Model-based (template-driven) metric 3D shape and motion estimation from MONOCULAR drone video, with an explicit TRANSMISSION MODEL to account for water-induced occlusion (partial submersion / attenuation). Downstream outputs are metric mass and volume estimates for body-condition assessment. The specific template — whether a SMAL derivative or a bespoke cetacean model — and its joint count are NOT stated in the abstract and I could not reach the full text (Springer blocked, arXiv blocked). The record's hedge on this was appropriate and I am preserving it rather than guessing. However, the senior author is SILVIA ZUFFI, the author of SMAL / SMALR / SMALST, which makes a SMAL-lineage articulated mesh the strong prior — and that in turn drags in SMAL's non-commercial, registration-gated licensing as a likely constraint. Treat as a lead to confirm, not a fact.
supervision: Monocular drone video of wild bottlenose dolphins captured under differing sea conditions; additionally applied to video of CAPTIVE animals with KNOWN GROUND-TRUTH MASS for quantitative validation. Compared against a manual 2D-measurements-based baseline.
species_domain: Bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops sp.), wild plus captive validation animals.
data_requirement: NOT STATED in any source I could reach. The abstract and arXiv metadata give no image counts, no individuals, no resolution, no training-set size and no GPU-hours; the arXiv version is only 9 pages / 7 figures, and the full IJCV text is behind Springer, which is blocked from this session. Number of views: MONOCULAR (single drone camera) — this is the one concrete and highly favorable input-regime fact, and it is the opposite of Neural Texture Puppeteer's 24-view rig.
key_numbers: IJCV 134(6):293 (2026); arXiv v1 9 pages, 7 figures. HEADLINE RESULT, verbatim from the published abstract and NOT captured in the candidate record: "While in our experiments the manual approach is often more accurate, our method demonstrates a distinct advantage when applied to larger specimen." I.e. the automated model-based pipeline LOSES to manual 2D photogrammetric measurement in most of their experiments, winning only on larger animals. Also verbatim, and directly citable as the field's own gap statement: "While considerable progress has been made in reconstructing 3D models of terrestrial quadrupeds, aquatic animals remain unexplored due to the difficulty of observing them in their natural underwater environment." No PA-MPJPE or any pose metric is reported — the evaluation is mass/volume, not pose or identity.
elongate_relevance: medium-high — closest match in body plan (fusiform, limbless), medium (through-water imaging, drone monocular) and capture modality, and it is the only marine model-based 3D reconstruction confirmed here; but it undulates DORSOVENTRALLY where a sevengill bends LATERALLY (bending axis differs by 90 degrees), it targets body condition rather than re-identification, and it contains NO surface UV mapping and NO pigmentation-pattern component at all.

citation: Malte Pedersen, Joakim Bruslund Haurum, Stefan Hein Bengtson, Thomas B. Moeslund. 3D-ZeF: A 3D Zebrafish Tracking Benchmark Dataset. IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2020, pp. 2426-2436.
license: MIT — but DECLARED ONLY IN THE README, not as a file. I fetched /LICENSE, /LICENSE.md and /license.txt on branch `master`: all 404. The README's License section reads verbatim: "All code is licensed under the MIT license, except for the pymotmetrics and torchvision code reference, which are subject to their respective licenses when applicable." Because there is no LICENSE file, GitHub shows no license badge and automated license scanners will report 'unknown'. SEPARATE ISSUE: this covers the CODE only. The 3D-ZeF20 DATASET is not in this repo — it is hosted on MOTChallenge (motchallenge.net/data/3D-ZeF20), and I could NOT verify the dataset's license because motchallenge.net is egress-blocked in this session. Do not assume the dataset is MIT.
representation_3d: NONE. 3D point trajectories only. Confirmed by reading the repo's own pipeline description: ExtractBackground.py -> BgDetector.py (2D bounding boxes + keypoint per view) -> TrackerVisual.py (2D tracklets) -> TrackletMatching.py (2D tracklets -> 3D tracklets by triangulation across two calibrated views) -> FinalizeTracks.py (full 3D tracks). The 3D content is entirely camera-calibration + triangulation: cam1/cam2 intrinsics JSON, world<->camera correspondence JSON, and .pkl calibrations built by reconstruction/JsonToCamera.py. There is no mesh, no SDF, no shape basis, no skinning, no UV parameterization, and no per-pixel depth anywhere in the codebase.
supervision: Fully supervised 2D. Annotated bounding boxes in AAU VAP format per view (used to train a Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 FPN backbone), plus per-view keypoint detections from background subtraction; identity association is evaluated with MOT metrics (py-motmetrics 1.1.3) against gt.txt / annotations_full.csv. 3D is obtained by geometric triangulation, not learned.
species_domain: Zebrafish (Danio rerio), laboratory glass tank, Aalborg, Denmark. Two orthogonal views (top = camT/cam1, front = camF/cam2).
data_requirement: Per-deployment requirement (verified from README): 2 synchronized calibrated video streams (cam1.mp4 top, cam2.mp4 front) plus cam1/cam2_intrinsic.json, cam1/cam2_references.json world<->camera correspondences, cam1/cam2.pkl calibrations, and a settings.ini. Faster R-CNN training expects train/ and valid/ image folders each with an annotations.csv. NUMBER OF FRAMES, RESOLUTION, FRAME RATE, SEQUENCE COUNT AND FISH-PER-SEQUENCE ARE NOT STATED ANYWHERE IN THE REPO — they live on the MOTChallenge 3D-ZeF20 page, which is egress-blocked here. I am deliberately not quoting numbers I could not fetch. GPU-hours: not stated. Pretrained Faster R-CNN weights are offered via a Dropbox link.
key_numbers: No performance numbers are stated in the repo README; the paper's MOTA/IDF1 figures were not fetchable (CVF Open Access and arXiv both egress-blocked). Verified structural facts only: 2 camera views, ResNet-50 FPN Faster R-CNN detector, py-motmetrics 1.1.3 evaluation.
elongate_relevance: low — it is a genuinely useful NEGATIVE control (the canonical 'fish + 3D' vision benchmark contains zero 3D geometry), but it offers nothing transferable to a laterally-bending, single-posterior-dorsal, seven-gill shark: no shape model to retarget, no surface to parameterize, and a two-orthogonal-camera tank rig that does not exist in field white-shark/sevengill video.
correction_note: CITATION IS CORRECT AS GIVEN — it matches the official BibTeX in the repo verbatim (@InProceedings{Pedersen_2020_CVPR}, IEEE/CVF CVPR, June 2020, all four authors in that order). Three corrections to the surrounding metadata: (1) the record's `url` points at the code repo, not the paper; the canonical venue record is the CVPR 2020 proceedings. (2) The license claim 'MIT (verified from repo)' is true in substance but should be qualified — there is NO LICENSE FILE, only a README sentence, so the repo has no machine-readable license. (3) The record asserts dataset properties as 'confirmed by reading the repo', but the dataset itself is not in the repo and its license and statistics were NOT verifiable in this session (motchallenge.net blocked). The 'no 3D geometry, only trajectories' claim IS confirmed from the code.

citation: Alzayat Saleh, Issam H. Laradji, Dmitry A. Konovalov, Michael Bradley, David Vazquez, Marcus Sheaves. A realistic fish-habitat dataset to evaluate algorithms for underwater visual analysis. Scientific Reports 10(1):14671, 2020. doi:10.1038/s41598-020-71639-x
license: MIT — VERIFIED by fetching the raw LICENSE file at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alzayats/DeepFish/master/LICENSE : standard MIT text, 'Copyright (c) 2019 Alzayat Saleh'. NOTE this covers the CODE. The DATASET is distributed separately from data.qld.edu.au (Queensland Government public data portal, collection Q5842) and from research.jcu.edu.au; I could NOT reach either host to read the data licence (both egress-blocked), so the dataset licence is UNVERIFIED — do not assume it is MIT. Also note the code depends on ElementAI/LCFCN, installed from git, whose license I did not check.
representation_3d: NONE — 2D only. Four task heads: clf (fish/no-fish), loc (point-level localization/counting), seg (segmentation masks), reg (count regression). No mesh, no shape model, no UV, no stereo, no per-pixel depth. IMPORTANT CORRECTION OF A LIKELY MISREADING: the paper/README does mention 'depth', but the README states verbatim that 'The depth and the map coordinates of the cameras were collected using an acoustic depth sounder and a GPS' — that is DEPLOYMENT WATER DEPTH as survey metadata, NOT depth imagery. There is no depth channel in the data.
supervision: Fully supervised 2D. Originally classification labels only; the authors then collected point-level annotations and segmentation masks to build the benchmark. Training entry point: `python trainval.py -e {loc,seg,clf,reg}`.
species_domain: Wild marine teleosts, 20 habitats in remote coastal tropical Australia. Cameras mounted on metal frames lowered from a vessel to the seabed and left recording the natural fish community with the vessel standing off 100 m; daylight hours, low-turbidity periods only.
data_requirement: VERIFIED FROM THE REPO README: 39,766 video frames total (the '~40 thousand images' figure), full HD 1920 x 1080, 20 habitats. The per-task subset sizes — how many of those 39,766 carry point-level annotations vs. segmentation masks — are NOT STATED in the README or anywhere I could reach; nature.com, alzayats.github.io and research.jcu.edu.au are all egress-blocked, so I am not quoting subset counts. Images per individual: N/A — this dataset has no individual identities at all, only fish/no-fish, points, and masks. Views: single monocular camera per deployment. GPU-hours: not stated.
key_numbers: 39,766 frames; 1920x1080; 20 habitats; 4 benchmark tasks (clf/loc/seg/reg). Reported accuracy figures were not fetchable (Nature blocked).
elongate_relevance: low — relevant only as a source of permissively-licensed real underwater fish SEGMENTATION MASKS to pretrain a silhouette-driven template fitter, which is exactly the supervision MagicPony/3D-Fauna consume. It contributes nothing about elongate bodies specifically (tropical Australian reef/estuarine teleosts, mostly fusiform-to-deep-bodied), nothing about hexanchiform morphology, and nothing about individual identity.
correction_note: PAPER EXISTS AND THE VENUE/YEAR/VOLUME/ARTICLE NUMBER ARE CORRECT — verified against the official BibTeX in the repo README (Scientific Reports, volume 10, number 1, pages 14671, 2020, doi 10.1038/s41598-020-71639-x). TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) the record's author list 'Alzayat Saleh, Issam H. Laradji, et al.' is truncated; the full canonical list is Saleh, Laradji, Konovalov, Bradley, Vazquez, Sheaves — Konovalov, Bradley and Sheaves (all JCU marine science) are the domain co-authors and dropping them misattributes the work as a pure ML paper. (2) The record says '~40k full-HD frames'; the exact figure stated by the authors is 39,766. I also flag that the record's '2D only, no depth' claim is right but the paper does use the word 'depth' for acoustic sounder water depth, which is an easy trap for a downstream reader.

citation: Zizhang Li, Dor Litvak, Ruining Li, Yunzhi Zhang, Tomas Jakab, Christian Rupprecht, Shangzhe Wu, Andrea Vedaldi, Jiajun Wu. Learning the 3D Fauna of the Web. IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2024. arXiv:2401.02400
license: MIXED / NOT CLEANLY MIT — THIS IS THE BIGGEST CORRECTION IN THIS CHUNK. The root LICENSE file (fetched raw) is genuine MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2023 Shangzhe Wu'. BUT the geometry and rendering core is vendored NVIDIA code carrying a PROPRIETARY header. I fetched model/render/mesh.py, model/render/render.py, model/render/texture.py and model/geometry/dmtet.py: all four begin with 'Copyright (c) 2020-2022 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved. NVIDIA CORPORATION, its affiliates and licensors retain all intellectual property and proprietary rights in and to this material... Any use, reproduction, disclosure or distribution of this material and related documentation without an express license agreement from NVIDIA CORPORATION or its affiliates is strictly prohibited.' render.py additionally says 'Adapted from NVDiffRec (https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrec), Modified by Shangzhe Wu for MagicPony in 2023'. On top of that, INSTALL.md makes two NVIDIA research-license packages HARD dependencies: `pip install git+https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrast/` and `pip install git+https://github.com/NVlabs/tiny-cuda-nn@v1.6` — nvdiffrast ships under the NVIDIA Source Code License (non-commercial research use only) and tiny-cuda-nn under a BSD-3-Clause-plus-NVIDIA-restrictions arrangement. NET EFFECT FOR THE LAB: treat this codebase as RESEARCH / NON-COMMERCIAL, not as MIT. The MIT grant covers Wu's own contributions; it does not and cannot relicense the NVIDIA-headered files or the NVIDIA dependencies. If anything derived from this ever needs to ship commercially or be relicensed to a partner, this needs a lawyer, not a README.
representation_3d: Hybrid SDF-mesh via DMTet (marching tetrahedra over a tetrahedral grid, adapted from NVIDIA Kaolin), plus a learned articulated skeleton with linear blend skinning, rendered with nvdiffrast. Verified config values: grid_res 256 (coarse 128 for iterations 0-500,000). NUANCED CORRECTION ON UV: the record's flat 'NO UV atlas mentioned anywhere' is not quite right. model/geometry/dmtet.py defines `map_uv(self, faces, face_gidx, max_idx)` and calls it as `uvs, uv_idx = self.map_uv(faces, face_gidx, num_tets*2)`; model/render/mesh.py carries v_tex / t_tex_idx throughout; obj.py writes texcoords; and INSTALL.md pip-installs `xatlas`. So UV coordinates DO exist. BUT — and this is the point that matters for the research question — that UV is a PROCEDURAL PER-TETRAHEDRON-FACE ATLAS SLOT derived from the tet grid index, i.e. a packing layout for rendering, NOT a semantic canonical surface parameterization. Because DMTet's extracted topology can change with the SDF, the same (u,v) does NOT denote the same anatomical point across two individuals or two frames. It is emphatically not DensePose/CSE-style correspondence. The genuinely reusable canonical object here is the shared 3D PRIOR SHAPE (`prior_shape`, the pan-category base mesh the memory bank conditions), and the repo does expose a `canonicalization` visualization mode that morphs a reconstruction from input pose to a pre-configured canonical pose — but the README states this mode is 'only supported for quadrupeds'. A pose-free UV identity space would have to be defined by the lab on that canonical mesh; it is not provided.
supervision: Single-view web images + instance masks + DINO self-supervised features. No 3D ground truth, no keypoint labels, no multi-view. Verified from the training loop: the Fauna batch is (input_image, mask_gt, mask_dt, mask_valid, flow_gt, bbox, bg_image, dino_feat_im, dino_cluster_im, keypoint, seq_idx, frame_idx) with train config `load_dino_feature: true`, `dino_feature_dim: 16`; losses include mask, rgb, flow and a dino_feat_im_loss, plus a DCDiscriminator on the memory-bank embedding. At TEST time the README states only RGB is required — DINO features are not needed, and masks are optional (used only for higher-precision test-time texture finetuning).
species_domain: 100+ QUADRUPED species. The README calls it 'a pan-category single-image 3D quadruped reconstruction model'. The Fauna Dataset is web video frames and images plus DOVE, APT-36K, Animal3D and Animals-with-Attributes. NO fish, NO aquatic animals, NO elasmobranchs.
data_requirement: VERIFIED FROM config/train_fauna.yaml AND config/model/fauna.yaml: input/output image size 256x256; batch_size 6; num_iters 900,000; single GPU by default (`gpu: 0`) with optional multi-GPU via `accelerate launch --multi_gpu`; random horizontal flip augmentation on. DMTet grid_res 256, coarse grid_res 128 for the first 500,000 iterations. Skeleton is HARD-CODED IN CONFIG: num_body_bones 8 (body_bones_mode `z_minmax_y+`, i.e. the body chain is laid out between the shape's min and max extent along z, slightly uplifted in +y), num_legs 4, num_leg_bones 3 — so 8 + 12 = 20 bones; legs are attached to the body chain from iteration 60,000 onward, with attachment joints found automatically unless pinned via legs_to_body_joint_indices; leg rotation is only unlocked at iteration 300,000; constrain_legs false for Fauna (true for MagicPony). IMAGES PER INDIVIDUAL: N/A / not applicable — the model has no notion of individual identity; it consumes unpaired single images. NUMBER OF VIEWS: 1 (single-view). EXACT FAUNA DATASET IMAGE COUNT AND SPECIES COUNT: not stated in the repo, and the paper (arXiv) and project page (kyleleey.github.io) are both egress-blocked here, so I am not quoting a figure. GPU-HOURS: not stated; 900k iterations at batch 6 and 256px is a multi-day single-GPU run by inspection, but the repo gives no number.
key_numbers: Verified config numbers only: 256x256 input, batch 6, 900,000 training iterations, DMTet grid 256 (coarse 128 to iter 500k), 20 bones (8 body + 4 legs x 3), dino_feature_dim 16. The paper's quantitative results (keypoint transfer / mask IoU vs. MagicPony, LASSIE, Hi-LASSIE) were NOT fetchable in this session.
elongate_relevance: medium — and this is a MORE FAVOURABLE read than the input record's blanket 'structurally poor', based on reading the actual config rather than the abstract. The body prior is NOT a quadruped-specific joint tree: it is 8 bones laid out along the shape's longest axis by `z_minmax`, which is close to exactly what an anguilliform sevengill trunk needs, and `num_legs` is a plain config integer that can be set to 0 (leg attachment and leg rotation are both gated behind iteration schedules that simply never fire). So the ARTICULATION prior is retargetable in principle. What does NOT transfer: (a) the shape/appearance prior and the memory bank are learned over quadrupeds, so there is no useful initialization for a shark and the pan-category memory bank is dead weight for a single species; (b) thin fin membranes — a pectoral, a tall single posterior dorsal, and an elongate heterocercal caudal upper lobe — are marginal to resolve in a 256^3 DMTet grid and are a known DMTet failure mode; (c) the `canonicalization` pose-morph, the one feature closest to the pose-invariant-UV research question, is explicitly quadruped-only; (d) nothing in this model addresses seven gill slits or the absent second dorsal, and no keypoint schema is used at all, so the white-shark 16-keypoint transfer problem is orthogonal here rather than solved. VERDICT FOR THE RESEARCH QUESTION: this is a credible training RECIPE and the best-maintained starting codebase, but it does not deliver pose-free UV pattern comparison out of the box, and its non-commercial NVIDIA encumbrance is a real constraint.
correction_note: PAPER EXISTS; CITATION, VENUE, YEAR AND THE FULL NINE-AUTHOR LIST IN THAT EXACT ORDER ARE ALL CONFIRMED against the official BibTeX in the authors' own repo (@InProceedings{li2024fauna, booktitle=CVPR, year=2024}) and against the README's arXiv badge (2401.02400). FOUR CORRECTIONS: (1) LICENSE IS WRONG AND THE ERROR IS DECISION-RELEVANT — 'MIT (verified from repo)' understates it; the root license is MIT but model/render/*.py and model/geometry/dmtet.py carry NVIDIA 'all rights reserved / distribution strictly prohibited without an express license agreement' headers, and nvdiffrast + tiny-cuda-nn are hard install-time dependencies under NVIDIA research licenses. Treat as non-commercial. (2) The 'NO UV atlas mentioned anywhere (verified)' claim is factually wrong — dmtet.map_uv exists, v_tex/t_tex_idx are threaded through the mesh class, texcoords are written to OBJ, and xatlas is a pip dependency. The SUBSTANTIVE point the record was reaching for still stands and I have restated it precisely: the UV is a tet-index-derived rendering atlas, not an identity-consistent semantic correspondence. (3) The record's `fetched_primary: false` / confidence 'probable' can be upgraded — I fetched the authors' official repo, its LICENSE, its INSTALL.md, its BibTeX, and its model/config source. I did NOT fetch the arXiv abstract or the CVPR proceedings page (both egress-blocked), so the ABSTRACT text itself remains unverified; everything I assert above comes from code and config I actually read. (4) The record's elongate_relevance is too pessimistic — it did not notice that the body skeleton is an 8-bone longest-axis chain with num_legs as a config knob, which is the single most transferable thing in the codebase for an elongate body.

citation: Shangzhe Wu, Ruining Li, Tomas Jakab, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi. MagicPony: Learning Articulated 3D Animals in the Wild. IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2023. arXiv:2211.12497
license: MIXED / NOT CLEANLY MIT — identical situation to 3D-Fauna, since both live in the same unified 3DAnimals repo. Root LICENSE is MIT 'Copyright (c) 2023 Shangzhe Wu'; but model/render/render.py is explicitly labelled 'Adapted from NVDiffRec (https://github.com/NVlabs/nvdiffrec), Modified by Shangzhe Wu for MagicPony in 2023' and carries the NVIDIA 'all rights reserved / distribution strictly prohibited without an express license agreement from NVIDIA' header, as do mesh.py, texture.py and geometry/dmtet.py; and INSTALL.md hard-requires nvdiffrast and tiny-cuda-nn v1.6 from NVlabs, which are NVIDIA-research-licensed (non-commercial). FLAG THIS: it is not a clean permissive stack. The original standalone MagicPony repo (elliottwu/MagicPony) has since been superseded by and redirects to this unified 3DAnimals codebase.
representation_3d: Category-specific DMTet hybrid SDF-mesh + articulated bones with blend skinning, learned from single-view in-the-wild images, rendered via nvdiffrast. Verified: grid_res 256, coarse 128 for iterations 0-100,000. Same UV situation as 3D-Fauna — a procedural tet-face atlas for rendering, not a semantic canonical surface parameterization. Same important nuance: there IS a per-category canonical prior shape, so a canonical surface exists as an object even though no identity-consistent (u,v) is defined on it.
supervision: Single-category image collection + instance masks + DINO features + optical flow (for video collections); no 3D ground truth, no keypoint supervision. At test time RGB alone suffices; masks optional for test-time texture finetuning.
species_domain: CATEGORY-SPECIFIC, one model per category. Released/trained categories per the README: horses, birds, giraffes, zebras, cows. Data provenance: horse_videos and bird_videos from DOVE; horse_combined adds Weizmann Horse Database + PASCAL + Horse-10; giraffe_coco, zebra_coco, cow_coco are filtered COCO subsets. No fish, no aquatic animals.
data_requirement: VERIFIED FROM config/train_magicpony_horse.yaml AND config/train_magicpony_bird.yaml AND config/model/magicpony.yaml: 256x256 in/out image size; batch_size 10; num_iters 140,000 for horse and 120,000 for bird — note this is ~6.4x fewer iterations than 3D-Fauna's 900,000, i.e. a single-category model is far cheaper to train, which is the practically relevant fact for a one-species sevengill effort. Skeleton hard-coded identically to Fauna: num_body_bones 8 with body_bones_mode `z_minmax_y+`, num_legs 4, num_leg_bones 3, legs attached from iteration 60,000, constrain_legs TRUE (Fauna sets it false). DMTet grid_res 256, coarse 128 for the first 100,000 iterations. CRITICAL PRACTICAL NOTE from the README: the small categories (giraffe, zebra, cow) are NOT trained from scratch — the authors explicitly instruct finetuning from a pretrained horse model because those datasets 'are much smaller'. That is the honest signal about how much data a new category needs. IMAGES PER INDIVIDUAL: N/A, no identity modelling. VIEWS: 1. elongate_relevance: LOW-to-MEDIUM, and the prior pass's critique is correct and worth keeping. Procrustes/GPA removes translation, rotation and uniform scale only - it does NOT remove articulated bending. For an anguilliform, laterally flexible sevengill trunk, body bend is a large non-shape variance source that GPA will dump straight into PC1/PC2, so an SSM fit to live or flexed animals becomes a bending model rather than an identity/shape model. It is only sound on canonically straight specimens, i.e. preserved or CT-scanned dead animals - which for Notorynchus cepedianus means you need scanned specimens you almost certainly do not have. Two further sevengill-specific problems the prior pass missed: (a) a landmark schema must be redefined from scratch anyway - the white-shark 16-keypoint Schema v2 is invalid here (no second dorsal, single dorsal set far posterior near the pelvics, seven gill slits not five, so second_dorsal_base/second_dorsal_tip have no homologue and gill_slit is one-of-seven and ambiguous); and (b) GPA landmarks are point coordinates, so even a perfect sevengill shape space carries ZERO surface texture - it cannot represent the dark-on-light speckle pattern that is the claimed identity signal. Useful as the offline 'where would a template mesh and its shape PCs come from' step; useless as the pose-invariant UV re-ID mechanism itself.

venue: Research software, SCI Institute, University of Utah. Repository created 2013-05-21, actively maintained (last update 2026-08-28), 133 stars / 36 forks. Peer-reviewed companion publications are advertised on the project website but were NOT verifiable in this session — see correction_note.

representation_3d: Particle-based (correspondence-point) statistical shape modeling: a dense set of corresponding particles is OPTIMIZED across an entire population under an entropy-based objective that balances per-shape surface sampling against population compactness, yielding a point-distribution model with PCA modes. Inputs are binary segmentation volumes or surface meshes. Crucially, correspondence is learned by optimization — it does NOT require hand-placed landmarks, which is the main practical difference from MorphoWeave.
supervision: Unsupervised with respect to landmarks: needs a population of segmented binary volumes or surface meshes in roughly consistent alignment. No images, no keypoints, no pose labels.

No specimen-count minimum, particle-count default, runtime, or hardware requirement was recoverable from the primary sources I could reach. data_requirement: Images per individual: N/A — this is a shape (mesh/volume) tool, not an image tool. Views: N/A. Resolution: not stated. Population size: not stated, but particle-based SSM is inherently a population method — it is meaningless below roughly a dozen specimens and the PCA modes are unreliable until N substantially exceeds the number of retained modes. GPU-hours: not stated; the optimizer is CPU-based. FOR THE ASKER: same hard blocker as MorphoWeave — zero sevengill surface meshes exist in the lab, and one great-white template mesh is not a population. ShapeWorks is the correct tool for a job the data does not yet permit.
elongate_relevance: low — this is the strongest MIT-licensed route to a sevengill shape space IF sevengill meshes ever existed, but two things count against it for this body plan. (1) Entropy-driven particle optimization on an elongate, near-cylindrical trunk produces axially sliding / degenerate correspondences: the surface-sampling term is happy anywhere along a featureless cylinder, so particle identity along the anterior-posterior axis is under-constrained — the same ill-posedness that makes a stable UV atlas hard on an eel-like body, which is the core risk to the asker's whole pose-invariant-UV premise. (2) The very long upper caudal lobe is a thin high-aspect-ratio extremity where particle splitting and correspondence collapse are known problems. I found NO published application of ShapeWorks to elongate fish or to any elasmobranch — searched the repo README and repository metadata; the project's own application list is psychology, biological phenotyping, cardiology and orthopedics (all compact/blobby anatomy). Treat any claim that ShapeWorks 'works on' shark-shaped geometry as unsupported.

elongate_relevance: low (indirect, but it is the cheapest way to resolve the highest-leverage unknown). Two cautions. citation: Neverova N., Novotny D., Khalidov V., Szafraniec M., Labatut P., Vedaldi A., "Continuous Surface Embeddings", NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2011.12438. Primary artifact verified here: DensePose CSE built-in mesh registry, facebookresearch/detectron2, projects/DensePose/densepose/data/meshes/builtin.py (main branch).
license: detectron2 (which contains the DensePose CSE project) = Apache-2.0 — VERIFIED by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/detectron2/main/LICENSE, title line 'Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004'. The SEPARATE legacy repo facebookresearch/DensePose = 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International Public License' — VERIFIED by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/facebookresearch/DensePose/main/LICENSE. NOT VERIFIED: the terms on the mesh .pkl assets and the CSE annotation JSONs themselves, which are served from dl.fbaipublicfiles.com and are not covered by the repo LICENSE files I read; DensePose-COCO/LVIS annotations derive from COCO/LVIS and carry their own terms. Treat the asset licensing as an open question, not as Apache-2.0.
representation_3d: Per-category canonical 3D mesh with a learned continuous surface embedding: the network predicts a 16-channel per-pixel embedding E plus 2-channel coarse segmentation; an embedder produces per-vertex embeddings Ê for the category mesh; pixel->vertex correspondence is nearest-neighbour matching in embedding space. CORRECTION to the input record: the claim 'not a UV atlas' is inaccurate as stated. Every registered mesh ships FOUR assets — data (.pkl), geodists/ (geodesic distance matrix), symmetry/, and texcoords/ — i.e. a UV parameterisation IS shipped per mesh. What is true is that correspondence is established via vertex embeddings + geodesic loss, not via a chart/UV regression as in original chart-based DensePose; texcoords are carried alongside for texture transfer/visualisation. Also noted from the source: horse_5004 reuses texcoords_zebra_5002.pkl (shared UV, or a registry copy-paste) — relevant if you were planning to trust shipped texcoords as species-specific.
supervision: Sparse image-to-vertex point annotations (dp_x, dp_y, dp_vertex, ref_model) plus polygon foreground masks. Animal models are obtained by FINETUNING a human CSE model on animal data, not trained from scratch — the cross-category transfer path is real but it transfers from a human/quadruped prior.
species_domain: VERIFIED by reading builtin.py in full — exactly 13 meshes, no more: smpl_27554, chimp_5029, cat_5001, cat_7466, sheep_5004, zebra_5002, horse_5004, giraffe_5002, elephant_5002, dog_5002, dog_7466, cow_5002, bear_4936. The CSE annotation datasets cover only 9 animal categories (bear, cow, cat, dog, elephant, giraffe, horse, sheep, zebra). Zero fish, zero elasmobranchs, zero aquatic species, zero limbless or elongate bodies. The input record's list was correct.
data_requirement: Concrete, read from DENSEPOSE_CSE.md and DENSEPOSE_DATASETS.md. Annotation density: ~3 image-to-vertex points per annotated instance for animals (vs ~100 points/instance for the human chart-based COCO set). DensePose-Chimps CSE: 500 instances / 350 images train, 430 instances / 304 images val. DensePose-LVIS ds1_train: 556 categories, 4141 images, 23985 segm overall; 9-animal subset 4141 images, 9472 segm, 5184 DensePose annotations. ds2_train: 1203 categories, 99388 images, 1270141 segm overall; animal subset 13746 images, 46964 segm, 18932 DensePose annotations. ds2_val: 2690 images, 9155 segm, 3604 DensePose annotations. Training cost (their reported numbers): 0.349–0.504 s/iter, 6.3–8.3 GB train memory, R_50/R_101 FPN backbones; animal finetune schedules are 4k or 16k iterations. Human CSE baseline dp.AP GPS 64.4–65.6, GPSm 65.7–66.6. Images-per-individual and number of views: NOT APPLICABLE / not stated — CSE is a correspondence task, not a re-ID task, and the datasets carry no individual identity labels at all.
elongate_relevance: low-to-negative — all 13 shipped meshes are compact-bodied tetrapods (human, ape, 8 quadruped mammals); the geodesic-distance embedding loss and the symmetry maps have never been validated on a limbless, laterally undulating, elongate body, and nothing in the ecosystem is aquatic. This is the single strongest NEGATIVE result for the sevengill question: to run CSE on Notorynchus cepedianus the lab would have to author the canonical mesh, the geodesic matrix, the symmetry map, the texcoords AND the image-to-vertex annotations from scratch, with no marine prior to finetune from and no white-shark asset either.
key_numbers: 13 built-in meshes; 9 annotated animal categories; 16-channel embedding; ~3 annotated points per animal instance; 5184 (ds1) / 18932 (ds2) animal DensePose annotations total; human CSE dp.AP GPS 64.4–65.6.
correction_note: Three corrections. (1) The record's '...not a UV atlas' is wrong as written — texcoords/*.pkl (a UV parameterisation) ships with every mesh; the accurate statement is that CORRESPONDENCE is via vertex embeddings + geodesic loss rather than chart/UV regression. (2) The record's citation was artifact-only; canonicalised to the actual NeurIPS 2020 CSE paper with arXiv:2011.12438 (ID read from the detectron2 doc's own link, since arxiv.org is egress-blocked in this session — I could not fetch the abs page). citation: Zuffi S., Kanazawa A., Berger-Wolf T., Black M.J., "Three-D Safari: Learning to Estimate Zebra Pose, Shape, and Texture from Images 'In the Wild'", International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) 2019. arXiv:1908.07201.
license: DUAL, and the non-commercial half dominates. LICENSE.txt = MIT (code). LICENSE_SMAL_MODEL.txt = MPI/MPG non-commercial research license — VERIFIED by fetching the full text (see the smal-model-license record): non-commercial research/education/artistic use only, no commercial ML training, no redistribution or transfer to third parties, modifications may not be shared without written MPI permission. THIRD, PREVIOUSLY-MISSED CONSTRAINT: the README instructs the user to 'obtain the SMPL model and place it in the smal_model directory' — SMPL carries its own separate MPI/MPG non-commercial license and its own registration/EULA on smpl.is.tue.mpg.de. So running SMALST requires clearing TWO independent MPI non-commercial EULAs on top of the MIT code.
representation_3d: SMAL template mesh with per-instance predicted shape, pose, camera AND texture. Texture is predicted directly in the template's UV space (the repo's data loader carries texture_map / texmap files and a uvflow field per training image), i.e. it produces a canonical, pose-free UV image of the animal's surface appearance.
supervision: Trained principally on SYNTHETIC images rendered from the textured SMAL zebra model, plus real images with masks and 2D keypoints. Test and validation sets are real photographs collected at The Great Grevy's Rally 2018. The code is a fork/derivative of akanazawa/cmr (README states this explicitly).
species_domain: Zebra (Grevy's zebra, Equus grevyi, per the Great Grevy's Rally provenance; the SMAL equine family more broadly). Single species, terrestrial quadruped.
data_requirement: Partly verified from the repo source, partly NOT VERIFIED. From the code (nnutils/train_utils.py, data/zebra.py): default num_images = 3000 training images, batch_size = 8, num_epochs default 1000 with num_train_epoch 40, learning rate 1e-4 (Adam, beta1 0.9), SINGLE GPU (a scalar gpu_id flag — no multi-GPU path), per-file texture maps enabled by default. From the README: pretrained weights are pred_net_186.pth (epoch 186); training/test/validation sets are downloaded from Google Drive; the runtime is Python 2.7 with PyTorch 0.5.0 — effectively unrunnable on a modern stack without a substantial port, which is a real, non-trivial engineering cost for the lab. NOT STATED anywhere I could reach: image/crop resolution, texture-map resolution, exact synthetic render count, GPU-hours, and the paper's quantitative results (IoU/PCK/keypoint error). I could NOT fetch the paper text: arxiv.org, openaccess.thecvf.com, api.semanticscholar.org, www.semanticscholar.org and huggingface.co are ALL blocked by this session's egress proxy (confirmed via the proxy status endpoint), and the WebSearch budget was exhausted before I could route around it. Anyone finalising this record should re-fetch arXiv:1908.07201 for the paper-reported numbers. Images per individual / number of views: not applicable — SMALST is single-image reconstruction and does not do identity matching; the zebra-stripe UV output is a means to re-ID, not a re-ID benchmark.
elongate_relevance: medium — the highest of the four for the actual research question, but with a serious caveat. SMALST is the strongest public existence proof that the mechanism the sevengill idea needs is buildable: predict a canonical-UV-space texture for a patterned animal from a single in-the-wild photo, using a template plus a synthetic-render training pipeline — which is structurally identical to what the lab already built for white sharks. The caveat is that a zebra's torso is near-rigid, so stripe geometry in UV space is stable almost for free. A sevengill's speckle pattern sits on an anguilliform trunk that bends laterally through large amplitudes, and the pattern's UV-space stability under that bending is an untested empirical question — SMALST provides no evidence either way. Additionally, none of SMALST's assets transfer: the template is equine, and the lab's 16-keypoint white-shark schema itself does not transfer to a sevengill (no second dorsal, single posterior dorsal near the pelvics, seven gill slits not five, elongate high-aspect upper caudal lobe), so second_dorsal_base, second_dorsal_tip and the single gill_slit landmark all need respecifying before any of this pipeline could even be pointed at the species.
key_numbers: 3000 default training images; batch size 8; lr 1e-4; single GPU; pretrained checkpoint at epoch 186; Python 2.7 / PyTorch 0.5.0. Paper-reported accuracy metrics NOT VERIFIED (sources egress-blocked).
correction_note: Citation, venue, year and author list all confirmed verbatim from the repo's own BibTeX block (@inproceedings{Zuffi:ICCV:2019}). Two substantive additions the input record missed: (1) a THIRD license dependency — the README requires downloading the SMPL model, which carries its own separate MPI non-commercial EULA and registration, on top of the SMAL model license and the MIT code; (2) the codebase is Python 2.7 / PyTorch 0.5.0, a material porting cost that the record's 'demonstrates the mechanism is buildable' framing understates. Also corrected the record's implicit claim of verified training details — the paper's own numbers could not be fetched (arxiv.org, openaccess.thecvf.com, semanticscholar and huggingface all egress-blocked); the numbers reported here are read from the repo source code, not the paper.

citation: 3DAnimals unified codebase (github.com/3DAnimals/3DAnimals) implementing three papers: (1) Wu S., Li R., Jakab T., Rupprecht C., Vedaldi A., "MagicPony: Learning Articulated 3D Animals in the Wild", CVPR 2023; (2) Li Z., Litvak D., Li R., Zhang Y., Jakab T., Rupprecht C., Wu S., Vedaldi A., Wu J., "Learning the 3D Fauna of the Web", CVPR 2024; (3) Sun K., Litvak D., Zhang Y., Li H., Wu J., Wu S., "Ponymation: Learning Articulated 3D Animal Motions from Unlabeled Online Videos", ECCV 2024.
venue: CVPR 2023 / CVPR 2024 / ECCV 2024 (single unified code release)
license: MIT. VERIFIED by fetching https://raw.githubusercontent.com/3DAnimals/3DAnimals/main/LICENSE — first lines read verbatim: "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2023 Shangzhe Wu". No non-commercial clause, no EULA, no registration wall. This is the only permissively-licensed option among the parametric-animal-model family (contrast SMAL/BITE/BARC, all MPI non-commercial). CAVEAT: the MIT license covers the CODE in this repo; the downloaded Fauna_dataset.zip and pretrained checkpoints are pulled from download.cs.stanford.edu and their terms are NOT stated in the repo — I could not reach that host to check, so treat dataset/checkpoint licensing as unknown.
representation_3d: Hybrid implicit-to-explicit: a learned category-level SDF on a DMTet tetrahedral grid, marching-tetrahedra-extracted to a mesh, plus a predicted articulation (learned bone/skinning) and a texture/albedo field. Confirmed from repo: config/ has a data/tets directory and DMTet grid assets. Learned per-category (MagicPony) or pan-category via a memory bank (3D-Fauna); no artist template mesh and no 3D ground truth required.
supervision: Single-view in-the-wild image collections plus off-the-shelf masks and self-supervised DINO features. Verified from configs: load_dino_feature: true, dino_feature_dim: 16. No 3D scans, no multi-view, no keypoint labels required at training time. At test time RGB alone suffices (masks and DINO features optional).
species_domain: CONFIRMED, and confirmed NEGATIVE for aquatic species. Repo config/ directory enumerates exactly: train/test_magicpony_horse, _bird, _cow, _giraffe, _zebra; train/test_ponymation_horse, _cow, _giraffe, _zebra; train/test_fauna (pan-quadruped). There is NO fish, shark, elasmobranch, cetacean or any aquatic config, dataset or checkpoint anywhere in the release. 3D-Fauna is described as pan-category for QUADRUPEDS specifically — the pan-category claim does not extend beyond tetrapods.
data_requirement: Concrete numbers read directly from the released training configs (the papers' own compute tables were not reachable — arxiv.org, huggingface.co, paperswithcode.com and kyleleey.github.io are all blocked by this session's egress proxy, so paper-stated GPU-hours are NOT verified). config/train_fauna.yaml: in_image_size 256, out_image_size 256, batch_size 6, num_iters 900000, gpu: 0 (single-GPU). config/train_magicpony_horse.yaml: image size 256/256, batch_size 10, total iterations 140000, gpu: 0 (single-GPU). So: 256x256 input resolution, single-GPU training, and ~900k iterations at batch 6 for the pan-category Fauna model — on the order of weeks of single-GPU time. Images per individual: NOT APPLICABLE / not stated — these methods train on unordered species-level image collections, not per-individual sets, and they do not do individual re-ID. Number of views: 1 (single-view, monocular). Total Fauna dataset size: not stated in any file I could reach; data/fauna/download_fauna_dataset.sh only wgets Fauna_dataset.zip from download.cs.stanford.edu with no size or category count given.
elongate_relevance: MEDIUM — genuinely the strongest positive methodological lead for the template problem, but with two concrete blockers for a sevengill. POSITIVE: it is the only credible published route to an articulated 3D template with no scanned mesh and no artist asset, which matters because (per the prior negative findings) no sevengill 3D asset appears to exist; and MIT licensing means no SMAL-style redistribution trap. BLOCKER 1: the articulation prior is a quadruped skeleton — a spine plus four limbs, learned from horses/cows/giraffes/zebras/birds. An anguilliform, laterally-undulating trunk with a single posterior dorsal, paired pectorals/pelvics and a long-upper-lobe heterocercal caudal is outside the learned bone topology entirely; nothing in the release validates a legless, elongate, laterally-bending body, and the 16-keypoint white-shark schema is irrelevant here anyway since the method uses no keypoints. BLOCKER 2 and the decisive one for THIS research question: DMTet meshes are re-extracted per instance by marching tetrahedra, so vertex count and connectivity are not guaranteed stable across instances and there is NO persistent, instance-consistent UV atlas by default. Pose-invariant re-ID by canonical (u,v) surface mapping requires exactly that fixed atlas. So 3DAnimals can plausibly give you a sevengill SHAPE, but it does not by itself give you the canonical UV coordinate frame the speckle-pattern re-ID idea depends on — you would have to add a UV parameterisation stage on top and prove it is consistent across individuals and poses.
key_numbers: Fauna training: 256x256, batch 6, 900,000 iterations, 1 GPU. MagicPony horse: 256x256, batch 10, 140,000 iterations, 1 GPU. DINO feature dim 16. Three papers, one repo. Five named MagicPony categories + one pan-quadruped model. Zero aquatic categories. Paper-reported reconstruction metrics NOT verified (arXiv blocked).

It also establishes the price of that route: roughly 12k labelled within-species images to learn the prior, which for sevengills is a corpus that does not exist. LIMITS: the dog-to-dog-breed jump is a shape-prior shift within one body plan. White shark (Lamniformes) to sevengill (Hexanchiformes) is not — it changes the fin inventory itself (no second dorsal; the single dorsal sits far posterior near the pelvics; seven gill slits instead of five; a strongly heterocercal caudal with a very long upper lobe; a much more elongate, laterally flexible anguilliform trunk). PCA over a shape space cannot delete a fin or move a gill slit count — those are topology/landmark-set changes, and they break the existing 16-keypoint white-shark schema outright: second_dorsal_base and second_dorsal_tip have no sevengill homologue, first_dorsal_base/tip land in a completely different body region, and a single gill_slit keypoint is under-specified for seven slits. Additionally the SMAL lineage's articulation is a quadruped spine-plus-four-legs rig; lateral undulation of an anguilliform trunk is not what that rig was built for. license: GPL (>= 3). NOW VERIFIED — the record said 'NOT VERIFIED'. Read verbatim from the License field of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/geomorphR/geomorph/master/DESCRIPTION. Copyleft, not permissive: GPL-3 obligations propagate to derived/linked work, which matters if the lab intends to ship a closed pipeline. No non-commercial clause and no registration wall, so it is commercially usable subject to GPL terms — a materially better licensing position than the SMAL/BITE family. Companion package RRPP (a hard dependency) is separately licensed; not checked.
representation_3d: Not a 3D reconstruction method — a statistical shape-analysis layer. Operates on configurations of homologous 2D or 3D landmarks, plus semilandmarks sliding on curves and on surfaces. Core pipeline is Generalized Procrustes Analysis (translation/rotation/scale removal) followed by PCA in tangent/Procrustes shape space, with allometry, phylogenetic and modularity/integration tests on top.
supervision: Fully supervised on manually placed homologous landmark coordinates per specimen. No learning, no images — you supply the digitised landmark configurations.
species_domain: Species-agnostic. It is the de facto standard statistical toolkit in fish and elasmobranch geometric morphometrics, which is exactly why it matters for reviewer acceptance in the marine-biology literature.
data_requirement: No training set, no GPU — this is CPU R code on landmark coordinate matrices. Requirement is instead statistical: n specimens x p landmarks x k dimensions, and the practical constraint is that p*k typically exceeds n (high-dimension-low-sample-size), which is why the package routes inference through RRPP permutation procedures rather than parametric MANOVA. The package does not state a minimum n; the field convention for a stable Procrustes mean and interpretable PC warps is on the order of tens of specimens per group. Images per individual: not applicable (1 standardised lateral photograph per specimen is the usual fish-morphometrics protocol). Views: 1 for 2D, or a 3D digitised surface/CT for 3D. Resolution: not stated. Package version read from DESCRIPTION: 4.1.1, dated 2026-07-04; the CITATION file references v4.1.0.
elongate_relevance: MEDIUM, as a vocabulary layer rather than a method. VALUE: if the lab wants a sevengill shape space that fish-biology reviewers will accept, Procrustes/PC-warps/allometry is the language they expect, and it is more defensible than ad-hoc PCA over raw vertex offsets (which is what SharkSMPL currently does). It also gives a principled way to define a NEW sevengill landmark schema rather than bending the 16-keypoint white-shark one — and a new schema is unavoidable given no second dorsal, a posterior single dorsal and seven gill slits. LIMIT — and this is the crux for a laterally-bending animal: GPA removes translation, rotation and scale, but it does NOT remove articulation. A free-swimming sevengill's lateral body undulation enters the Procrustes residual as apparent SHAPE variance and will dominate the leading PCs, confounding pose with identity — precisely the confound this whole research question is trying to escape. This is why elongate-fish landmark schemes are conventionally digitised from straightened or preserved specimens, which is not an option for a live-video re-ID pipeline. So geomorph is useful for describing sevengill shape from controlled/straightened material, but it does NOT solve pose-invariance for in-water video, and it offers no surface (u,v) parameterisation at all.

citation: Baken, E.K., Collyer, M.L., Kaliontzopoulou, A., Adams, D.C. geomorph v4.0 and gmShiny: Enhanced analytics and a new graphical interface for a comprehensive morphometric experience.
