representation_3d: Canonical neural implicit shape (SDF/occupancy + appearance) in a fixed canonical space, plus a learned skeleton and neural blend skinning, optimised jointly across many casual monocular videos. Canonical surface embeddings / feature fields provide the video-to-canonical correspondence that registers frames from different videos into ONE canonical space. RAC extends this to a CATEGORY-level model: a shared canonical body plus per-instance shape codes and per-instance skeleton scale - effectively a learned SMAL-analogue built from video instead of from scans.
supervision: Monocular video plus segmentation masks, optical flow, and long-range 2D correspondence / self-supervised surface features (DensePose-CSE or DINO-style features, depending on version). No 3D scans, no rigged template, no manual keypoints.
species_domain: Cats, dogs, humans (BANMo); category-level cat/dog/human models (RAC). All terrestrial quadrupeds and bipeds; no fish, no elongate swimmers, no underwater imagery.
data_requirement: From the official BANMo repo README (verified): preprocessed subjects are 'cat-pikachiu' = 11 videos and 'human-cap' = 10 videos, plus dog-tetres and cat-coco; the short training schedule takes 4 hours on 2x V100 GPUs (plus SSD storage) and the full higher-quality schedule takes 12 hours on 2x V100 - i.e. roughly 8 to 24 GPU-hours per subject. Marching-cubes output resolution is configurable up to 256^3. Input image resolution and exact per-video frame counts are NOT stated in the README. RAC's own numbers (number of category videos, number of instances) could NOT be verified: the RAC project page (gengshan-y.github.io) is egress-blocked and arxiv.org is egress-blocked, so I am not quoting a figure for it - not stated in any source I could reach. elongate_relevance: high in principle, unproven in practice, and this is the honest tension. It is the most credible route to a sevengill canonical model given the hard constraint that no rigged Notorynchus template and no Notorynchus scan exists: RAC builds both the category template AND the per-individual shape space from video alone, which is exactly the missing asset. It is MIT (lab4d), actively maintained, and it consumes segmentation masks and optical flow - the lab already computes optical flow as channels 17-18 of the 19-channel proxy input, so integration cost is genuinely low. Against that: (1) the learned skeleton discovery has only ever been demonstrated on quadrupeds and humans, never on an anguilliform swimmer, and there is no published evidence it recovers a sensible axial chain for a laterally-undulating body; (2) the correspondence supervision (CSE/DINO-style surface features) is far weaker on a low-contrast grey-brown shark flank in turbid green water than on a patterned housecat in a living room - though note the sevengill's speckled/spotted pigmentation is actually MORE feature-rich than a white shark's, which cuts slightly in favour here; (3) it needs many videos of the SAME individual to build an instance, whereas encounter data typically gives one short pass per sighting; (4) an anguilliform trunk with a single far-posterior dorsal and a very long heterocercal upper caudal lobe is a topology and articulation regime the released configs do not cover, so the joint count and skinning priors would have to be re-specified - the white-shark 16-joint schema (with its second-dorsal pair and five-gill-slit convention) is not a usable starting point.

citation: Richard Izzo, David Steinman, Simone Manini, Luca Antiga. "The Vascular Modeling Toolkit: A Python Library for the Analysis of Tubular Structures in Medical Images." Journal of Open Source Software 3(25):745, 26 May 2018. DOI: 10.21105/joss.00745. [THIS is the verified, citable primary reference for VMTK. The record's proposed underlying-method citation - Antiga & Steinman, "Robust and objective decomposition and mapping of bifurcating vessels", IEEE TMI 2004 - could NOT be verified in this session and MUST NOT be shipped as-is; see correction_note.]
venue: Journal of Open Source Software (peer-reviewed), vol. 3, issue 25, article 745
license: BSD for VMTK itself - verified by reading the raw consolidated LICENSE file. Exact terms: BSD License, copyright 2004-2018 Luca Antiga, David Steinman, Simone Manini, Richard Izzo. The same LICENSE file enumerates bundled third-party components: Pypes (BSD, Antiga & Steinman 2004-2018), ITK (Apache-2.0 for v4+, BSD for v3.6), VTK (BSD), OpenNL (modified BSD, Bruno Levy), TetGen (modified MIT, Hang Si - flagged in the file itself as NOT a required dependency and as requiring a direct arrangement with the author for commercial use), Stellar/Starbase (BSD, portions public domain), and Python (PSF v2). Net: permissively licensed and commercially usable, with the one caveat that TetGen must be excluded from a commercial build (it is optional).
representation_3d: Centerline extraction on a tubular surface via Voronoi-diagram shortest paths, followed by 'branch mapping'. Verified directly from the source of vmtkScripts/vmtkbranchmapping.py, whose own description string reads: 'Constructs a harmonic function over each vascular segment; maps and stretches the longitudinal metric to correctly account for the presence of insertion regions at bifurcations; the additional StretchedMapping array is added to the surface.' Its inputs are the surface, the centerlines and a set of reference systems, together with Abscissas, ParallelTransportNormals, GroupIds, CenterlineIds, TractIds, MaximumInscribedSphereRadius, Blanking and AbscissaMetric arrays; its outputs are HarmonicMapping, BoundaryMetric and StretchedMapping arrays on the surface. In other words: each branch is harmonically mapped onto a canonical (longitudinal abscissa, circumferential angle) parametric domain so that data measured on different vessels, at different bends, are directly comparable in one fixed coordinate system.
supervision: None. Deterministic computational geometry and image processing - no learning, no training data, no labels.
species_domain: Human vascular anatomy from medical imaging (CT/MR angiography); cerebral aneurysms, carotid bifurcations, aortas.
data_requirement: No training data and no GPU: this is a deterministic geometry pipeline, so images-per-individual, views and GPU-hours are all not applicable. The real requirement is different in kind and should be stated as such: VMTK consumes an already-reconstructed, closed, watertight 3D surface mesh of the tubular structure. It presupposes the reconstruction step. For the shark problem that is the entire unsolved part - the lab has 661 GB of monocular video and no 3D reconstruction, so VMTK is a downstream parameterisation tool that cannot be applied until something (SharkSMPL fitting, or lab4d/RAC) produces a mesh. Runtime is seconds-to-minutes per surface on CPU; the repo states no benchmark figures.
elongate_relevance: high - maximally relevant to the body plan, and arguably the single most transferable idea in this chunk, but with a real prerequisite gap. Two carry-overs. (1) BEND INVARIANCE BY CONSTRUCTION: arc-length along a centerline and angle around it are unchanged by lateral undulation, so a (abscissa, circumferential angle) domain is pose-free for the trunk WITHOUT any learned deformation field. For an anguilliform, laterally-flexible sevengill trunk that is exactly the right invariance, and it sidesteps the canonical-space-drift problem that sinks Nerfies-style approaches for identity work. (2) NEAR-ISOMETRY: a generalized cylinder is developable, so flattening the trunk introduces little area distortion - important because a stretched map corrupts the spot/speckle geometry that is supposed to carry identity. Distortion concentrates at branch points, which on a shark means fin insertions, the head, and the caudal peduncle - and VMTK's branch-decomposition and 'stretched mapping' machinery exists precisely to handle those insertion regions. Caveats to state plainly: (a) it needs a 3D surface as input, which the pipeline does not yet produce; (b) the circumferential origin is defined only up to a rotation unless anchored to an anatomical reference - for a shark, the dorsal midline ridge or the lateral line, and the lateral line is the natural choice; (c) a shark trunk is a strongly non-circular, dorsoventrally-compressed cross-section, not a vessel-like near-circular tube, so the maximum-inscribed-sphere machinery will need adaptation; (d) the sevengill's single far-posterior dorsal and long heterocercal caudal upper lobe are branch structures with no vascular analogue in the shipped configs. Separately: this framing makes the white-shark 16-keypoint schema's inadequacy concrete - abscissa needs anatomical anchors that actually exist on Notorynchus, so second_dorsal_base and second_dorsal_tip must be dropped, first_dorsal_* re-anchored far posterior near the pelvics, and the single gill_slit landmark redefined for seven slits.

Verified functional primitives in vmtkbranchmapping.py: HarmonicMapping, BoundaryMetric, StretchedMapping output arrays; Abscissas + ParallelTransportNormals + GroupIds + TractIds inputs. JOSS paper: vol 3, issue 25, page 745, 2018-05-26.
